tourist_spots.name: Hundred Islands National Park (Governor's, Quezon, Marcos, Children's & Pilgrimage Islands)
tourist_spots.location: Off the coast of Barangay Lucap, Alaminos City, 2404 Pangasinan (Pilgrimage Island Plus Code: 626R+5F4; Phone: +63 75 433 7532 / +63 998 597 5153)
tourist_spots.fee_in_venue: Environmental Fee: PHP 40.00/person (Day Tour) or PHP 80.00/person (Overnight; kids <=5 free). Entrance/Registration Fee: PHP 30.00/person (Day Tour) or PHP 40.00/person (Overnight) + PHP 10.00 insurance fee. Motorboat Rental (Round-trip): Small (1–5 pax) PHP 1,400–1,600 Day / PHP 2,000–3,000 Overnight; Medium (6–10 pax) PHP 1,800 Day / PHP 3,800 Overnight; Large (11–15 pax) PHP 2,000 Day / PHP 4,500 Overnight. Activities: Governor's Island 546m Zipline PHP 250; Quezon Island 120m Zipline PHP 100; Helmet Diving PHP 400; Banana Boat PHP 250/head; Kayaking PHP 250/hr; Snorkeling Gear PHP 250/set.
tourist_spots.description: Established in 1940 as the first national park in the Philippines, Hundred Islands National Park spans roughly 1,844 hectares across the Lingayen Gulf and comprises 124 coral-limestone, mushroom-shaped islets at low tide (123 at high tide). Key developed islands include Quezon Island (white sand, activity centers, and a statue of President Manuel L. Quezon), Governor's Island (featuring a 180-step climb to a panoramic view deck and a 546-meter island-to-island zipline to Virgin Island), Marcos Island (home to Imelda's Cave and a 20-foot indoor cliff jump into clear lagoon water), Children's Island (shallow, shaded waters for kids), and Pilgrimage Island (Martha Island), which features a 1,400-step Way of the Cross leading to the towering Christ the Savior statue.
what_to_do: Go island hopping across 7+ developed islands including Quezon, Governor's, Marcos, Children's, Scout, Cuenco, and Pilgrimage Islands
Snorkel over giant clam (Taklobo) sanctuaries and vibrant coral gardens or try helmet diving
Ride the 546-meter island-to-island zipline from Governor's Island to Virgin Island and the 120-meter zipline on Quezon Island
Take the 20-foot indoor cave cliff jump inside Imelda's Cave on Marcos Island
Kayak, ride banana boats, jet ski, camp overnight, or climb the 1,400-step Way of the Cross to the Christ the Savior statue on Pilgrimage Island

tourist_spots.name: Bued Mangrove Park (Bued Mangrove Forest Eco-Park)
tourist_spots.location: 52C6+VC9, Barangay Bued, Alaminos City, Pangasinan, Philippines (open daily 7:30 AM – 4:30 PM)
tourist_spots.fee_in_venue: Free admission to walk along the mangrove boardwalk, take pictures, and relax; paid parking lot/street parking (cash-only) and optional fees for bamboo rafting or guided mangrove planting.
tourist_spots.description: Spanning 8.17 hectares in Barangay Bued, Bued Mangrove Forest Eco-Park is an award-winning coastal conservation project that transformed a barren, muddy river mouth into a thriving mangrove nursery and sanctuary. It is home to 22 true mangrove species and features a 448-meter-long elevated bamboo and concrete boardwalk, a two-to-three-story viewing gazebo overlooking the Lingayen Gulf, and a Tourism Satellite Office that serves as an alternate, less-crowded jump-off point for Hundred Islands tours.
what_to_do: Walk the 448-meter elevated boardwalk through dense coastal mangrove forests
Enjoy panoramic views of the mangrove canopy and Lingayen Gulf from the multi-story viewing gazebo
Go birdwatching, bamboo rafting, or join a mangrove seedling planting activity

tourist_spots.name: Saint Joseph the Patriarch Cathedral Parish (Alaminos Cathedral)
tourist_spots.location: 5X4H+6G7, CP Garcia St, Barangay Poblacion, Alaminos City, 2404 Pangasinan, Philippines (Coordinates: 16°09′20″N 119°58′43″E; Phone: +63 75 696 0391)
tourist_spots.fee_in_venue: Free admission; PHP 20.00 motorcycle parking fee in the church parking area.
tourist_spots.description: Founded in 1776 by the Augustinian Recollects and rebuilt in stone between 1837 and 1857 under Fr. Manuel Busqueto and Fr. Jose Tornos, the church was elevated to the episcopal seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Alaminos in 1985. The Baroque structure features a three-level retablo-style facade with a wing-like undulating wall concealing the aisle roof, segmented arch windows, a marble altar and floor, ceiling paintings, three gold-colored interior retablos, a grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes sculpted by Archbishop Mariano Madriaga, and a perpetual adoration chapel.

tourist_spots.name: Cape Bolinao Lighthouse
tourist_spots.location: 8Q4P+V64, Punta Piedra Point, Patar Road, Barangay Patar, Bolinao, 2406 Pangasinan
tourist_spots.fee_in_venue: Free admission to the lighthouse grounds and viewing deck (covered by the PHP 40.00 Bolinao Municipal Environmental/User's Fee pass valid for 4 days); small local parking fee applies outside.
tourist_spots.description: Built in 1903–1905 by Filipino, American, and British engineers atop the 351-foot (107-meter) limestone promontory of Punta Piedra Point in Barangay Patar, the 30.78-meter-tall (101-foot) octagonal Cape Bolinao Lighthouse is the second-tallest historic lighthouse in the Philippines (after Cape Bojeador). For over a century it has guided ships navigating the West Philippine Sea and offers sweeping views of Patar's golden coast and turquoise waters.

reviews.comment: The Cape Bolinao Lighthouse in Patar, Bolinao, Pangasinan, Philippines, is a historic, white-painted landmark built in 1905, standing over 100 meters high on Punta Piedra Point, offering stunning panoramic views of the West Philippine Sea.

tourist_spots.name: Enchanted Cave
tourist_spots.location: 8RV3+6RC, Patar Rd, Barangay Patar, Bolinao, 2406 Pangasinan (Phone: +63 998 577 4303; Open daily 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM)
tourist_spots.fee_in_venue: PHP 150.00–200.00 Entrance Fee (sightseeing/picture-taking) + PHP 50.00–100.00 Swimming Fee inside the cave (PHP 200.00–250.00 total per person); PHP 30.00 Parking Fee; Life vest rental available. On crowded weekends, cave swimming is regulated in 30-minute batches.
tourist_spots.description: Located along Patar Road inside an elevated coral reef park carpeted with millions-of-years-old fossilized giant clams and coral stones, Enchanted Cave is Bolinao's most famous subterranean spring pool. Visitors descend a narrow stairway into a dimly lit limestone cavern filled with crystal-clear, cool natural spring water (3 to 6 feet deep). The surrounding park also features a mini-zoo, giant clam shell displays, outdoor swimming pools, hammocks, and cliffside ocean views.

Swim in the outdoor surface pools or relax in shaded hammocks and cottages

Interior tours of the Capitol building and Urduja House can be coordinated through the Pangasinan Provincial Tourism and Cultural Affairs Office during weekday office hours.
tourist_spots.description: Built between 1917 and 1918 under American architect Ralph Harrington Doane during the term of Governor Daniel Maramba, the American Neoclassical Pangasinan Provincial Capitol features a limestone-and-concrete facade with Greek Corinthian columns, Roman military eagle emblems, a grand winding hardwood staircase, and a multicolored dancing fountain. Across from the Capitol stands Urduja House (built in 1953 under Governor Juan Rodriguez), the official residence and ceremonial reception hall of the Governor of Pangasinan, named after the legendary 14th-century warrior Princess Urduja of the Kingdom of Tawalisi and housing prized portraits of Urduja by Fernando Amorsolo and Antonio Gonzalez Dumlao (1954). Adjacent is the 1927 neoclassical Sison Auditorium.
what_to_do: Photograph the neoclassical facade, Corinthian columns, and grand interior staircase of the Provincial Capitol Building
Watch the multicolored dancing water fountain light up at night in front of the Capitol
Visit Urduja House to view its Balinese/Southeast Asian-inspired woodwork and portraits of Princess Urduja by Fernando Amorsolo and Antonio Dumlao
Stroll through the landscaped Aguedo Agbayani Park, Sison Auditorium grounds, and the Capitol beachfront promenade

tourist_spots.description: Unveiled in 2008 by Lingayen native and former Philippine President Fidel V. Ramos, Veterans Memorial Park is an open-air World War II memorial park commemorating the January 9, 1945 Allied Amphibious Landings at Lingayen Gulf led by Gen. It features the Lingayen Gulf Landing Shrine, vintage WWII fighter planes, two Cessna aircraft, tanks, naval cannons, wartime photography, and a replica of James Turnbull's 1945 painting Spirit of '45. Nearby in the town proper stands the restored Spanish-era Casa Real, now home to the Banáan Pangasinan Provincial Museum, which curates interactive galleries of Pangasinan's history, WWII heritage, ethnography, and contemporary art.

View historical photographs of Gen. Douglas MacArthur's S-Day landing and the Spirit of '45 mural replica
Take a guided tour through the galleries of the historic Casa Real at Banáan Pangasinan Provincial Museum

tourist_spots.name: Dawel River Cruise
tourist_spots.location: 386Q+3PH, Dawel Bridge Ferry Landing / Wharf, Brgy. Bonuan Boquig, Dagupan City, 2400 Pangasinan (Contact: Dagupan City Tourism Office, +63 75 515 6196)
tourist_spots.fee_in_venue: Free during city government promotional and Bangus Festival runs; prior reservation and schedule verification with the Dagupan City Tourism Office (+63 75 515 6196) is required. Open daily 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM.
tourist_spots.description: Launched by the Dagupan City Government to showcase the city's seven river systems and estuarine wetlands, the Dawel River Cruise takes up to 30 passengers aboard thatch-roofed bamboo rafts and motorboats on a 45-minute journey along the emerald waters of the Dawel-Watac-Mamalingling River. Starting at the Dawel Bridge wharf—decorated with colorful giant bangus sculptures—the cruise passes dense mangrove swamps, migratory herons, and traditional fishponds where world-famous Dagupan bangus (milkfish), malaga (siganid), and pompano are bred and harvested.
what_to_do: Take a 45-minute scenic boat tour aboard thatch-roofed river cruisers through Dawel River's coastal wetlands
Witness live bangus (milkfish) harvesting in riverside fish pens and fingerling release activities
Participate in community mangrove seedling planting and watch migratory birds (such as herons) along the riverbanks
Enjoy freshly grilled inihaw na bangus, small crabs, and native rice cakes (kakanin) on the raft or at the Dawel Bridge wharf, and snap photos with the colorful giant bangus sculptures

tourist_spots.name: Saints Peter and Paul Parish Church (Calasiao Church)
tourist_spots.location: 2964+2P4, Poblacion West (along Judge Jose de Venecia Sr. Ave / Mamaradlo St), Calasiao, 2418 Pangasinan

tourist_spots.description: Founded in 1588 by Dominican missionaries and constructed in Baroque style between the 17th and 19th centuries using massive coral stones and bricks (measuring 88 meters long and 27–30 meters high), the Saints Peter and Paul Parish Church is the second-oldest church in Pangasinan and a declared National Cultural Treasure by the National Museum of the Philippines and the NCCA. It features a five-story octagonal bell tower, an 18-post saint-lined quadrangle, a three-leveled classic retablo altar, and sits directly across from the Señor Divino Tesoro Shrine (2954+JM2) and the famous Puto Calasiao vendor stalls.

Attend Mass and light candles at the adjacent Señor Divino Tesoro Shrine across the street
Walk the forecourt quadrangle lined with 18 stone posts bearing statues of saints and explore the historic convent on the left side of the church
Buy freshly steamed Puto Calasiao (white, kutsinta, ube, pandan, and cheese flavors) from the row of stalls right outside the church plaza

tourist_spots.description: Inaugurated on April 5, 2019 to commemorate the 405th Founding Anniversary of Bayambang, the 400th year of the St. Vincent Ferrer Parish, and the 600th death anniversary of St. Vincent Ferrer, this towering 50.23-meter (164.8-foot) monument holds the official **Guinness World Record for the Tallest Bamboo Sculpture** in the world (surpassing the Statue of Liberty's 46-meter statue height without its pedestal and Brazil's 38-meter Christ the Redeemer). Privately funded by the Kasama Kita sa Barangay Foundation (spearheaded by former Mayor Cezar Quiambao and Nina Jose-Quiambao) with zero municipal funds spent, the monument was designed by JQS Builders using 3D polygon technology (~5,000 polygons, including 700 polygons for the saint's curly hair) and engineered by Far East Industrial Supply & Co. and RAA Architects Engineers and Consultants. Its interior frame utilizes 600 tons of structural steel clad with 60 tons (22,626 panels) of treated engineered bamboo imported from China, anchored on a 7.5-meter-deep foundation poured with 768.99 cubic meters of 6,000-psi concrete to withstand typhoons and earthquakes. Surrounding the monument is a landscaped prayer park featuring an air-conditioned hilltop chapel, meditation gardens, the *Jesus Way to Resurrection* / Stations of the Cross statues, spacious parking, and a food court.

tourist_spots.location: Barangay Batchelor East, Natividad, 2446 Pangasinan (Google Maps Place ID: `ChIJZSf_0DcckTMR1vE3tZjLkFw`; Phone: `+63 965 119 4216`)

tourist_spots.description: Tucked inside the forested Caraballo foothills of Barangay Batchelor East just beyond Sky Plaza, **Maranum Falls** takes its name from the Pangasinan/Ilocano word *"maranum"* ("abundant in water"), reflecting the fact that its strong mountain cascade never dries up even during the peak summer months. Feeding into the rocky Viray River, the waterfall drops into a wide, refreshing natural basin surrounded by lush tropical foliage and massive boulders. The trail from the inner registration gate takes about 10–15 minutes on foot (or ~30–45 minutes from the lower Sky Plaza jump-off) along pathways equipped with safety handrails and wooden stairs. To keep the water pristine, a strict municipal ordinance prohibits bringing food and alcoholic beverages inside the waterfall zone (drinking water and non-alcoholic beverages are allowed).
